home.title: Nuovo Hotel Faro – Seafront hotel in Capo d'Orlando, Sicily
home.description: Seafront hotel in Capo d'Orlando, beneath the lighthouse and facing the Aeolian Islands. Sea-view rooms, terrace breakfast, steps from the town centre.
home.heroText: On the Capo d'Orlando seafront, at the foot of the lighthouse and facing the Aeolian Islands.
home.introTitle: The sea below your window, the town centre a short walk away
intro: Nuovo Hotel Faro (2 stars, 43 beds) overlooks the Tyrrhenian Sea, facing the Aeolian Islands, on the beautiful seafront of Capo d'Orlando, just steps from the town centre.
It is a two-hour drive from Palermo and Catania airports, one hour by motorway from Cefalù and 900 metres from the railway station.

hotel.title: The Hotel – Nuovo Hotel Faro Capo d'Orlando
hotel.description: Nuovo Hotel Faro on the Andrea Doria seafront, below Monte Santuario: bar, breakfast room, sun terrace, TV room and garage.
hotel.lead: Nuovo Hotel Faro stands on the “Andrea Doria” seafront, at the foot of Monte Santuario. The headland and the legendary lighthouse make the surroundings enchanting and magical.
body: Guests are lulled by the sound of the sea and the cry of the gulls circling the lighthouse tower, the fishermen's “sentinel” and symbol of Capo d'Orlando.
In the morning you can enjoy a generous, varied breakfast of quality artisan products, in the cosy indoor room or in the flower-filled outdoor room with its relaxing sea view.
On the sun terrace we host sunset aperitif dinners with music and views of the Aeolian Islands.
services: Garage for cars, motorbikes and bicycles
hotel.extra: Through our partner agencies you can hire cars, motorbikes and boats and book organised tours of Sicily and the Aeolian Islands.

territorio.title: The Area – What to see in Capo d'Orlando
territorio.description: Capo d'Orlando and surroundings: the lighthouse, the Sanctuary, Villa Piccolo, Castello Bastione, the Roman baths of Bagnoli, the Nebrodi Park and the Aeolian Islands.
territorio.lead: Capo d'Orlando is the main tourist and shopping town of the Nebrodi area, on the north-eastern coast of Sicily, 100 km from Messina.
body: It boasts 5 km of lovely coastline, from the promenade to San Gregorio, an old fishing village and the most striking stretch, with rocks shaped by the sea over thousands of years.

The town is framed by green hills dotted with historic villages such as Naso and San Marco d'Alunzio, and is about an hour from Cefalù, Santo Stefano di Camastra, Milazzo and Taormina. On the horizon: the Aeolian Islands, the “seven sisters”.
Visiting Capo d'Orlando means living the sea in every way: swimming, sunbathing, long beach walks, fishing, reading on the rocks in the summer breeze and beach parties.
excursions: Aeolian Islands, departing from Capo d'Orlando or Milazzo
Nearby historic villages, rich in art and tradition

places.name: The Lighthouse
places.text: Together with the Madonna's mount, the town's symbol and a landmark for fishermen. Designed by the Genio Civile and lit in 1904, it has a square pink tower and shows a white light in groups of two every 12 seconds. It is just a few metres from the hotel.

places.name: The Castle and the Sanctuary
places.text: Legend says it was founded by Charlemagne in honour of the paladin Orlando. In the 16th century the tower watched for corsairs; the castle ruins were restored in 1994.

places.name: The Madonna of the Sanctuary
places.text: On 22 October 1598 a pilgrim, believed to be Saint Cono, left a small statue of the Madonna with the castle guards. Since 1600 a solemn feast with a market and fair has been held every 22 October.

places.name: Villa Piccolo Museum Foundation
places.text: Home of the Piccolo siblings, where Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa wrote much of The Leopard. It holds paintings, photographs, watercolours, ceramics and the poet Lucio Piccolo's famous dog cemetery.

places.name: Castello Bastione
places.text: The “sugar-mill tower”, probably built in the 14th century to protect sugar-cane plantations from pirate raids, now owned by the town.

places.name: Roman Baths of Bagnoli
places.text: 3 km from the centre, the remains of a Roman bath complex with frigidarium, tepidarium, calidarium and mosaic floors.

places.name: Mercadante Quarries
places.text: At San Gregorio, at low tide, large sandstone discs carved into the rock emerge; their purpose is still unknown.

places.name: Dragon Fountain
places.text: On the SS113 at Santa Lucia, a sandstone fountain decorated with majolica tiles from the Naso school, probably from the late 17th to early 19th century.

places.name: Nebrodi Park
places.text: Sicily's largest protected natural area: Mangalaviti Wood, Lake Biviere, Rocche del Crasto, the Springs Trail and the Catafurco Waterfall.
